title: Same badge twice
model_restatement: Say True if any name appears more than once, otherwise False.

clarify.question: Could the same person be spelled differently?
clarify.answer: No — names are clean and lowercase today.

clarify.question: Do you want who signed in twice?
What if the list is empty or has one name?
clarify.answer: Then nobody signed in twice — False.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Compare every name with every name after it. If any two match, someone signed in twice. Print the answer.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — iteration 4 (the second ana): after line 5, what is dup?

why_line: Comparing only neighbours checks ana–ben, ben–cy, cy–ana. The two anas are three seats apart, so no neighbour pair ever matches.

explain.rule: Checking only the next seat is a bouncer who remembers one face — the second ana walks in three people later and he's forgotten her.
explain.bridge: So what could remember EVERY name you've seen so far?

fix.rule: A set remembers every name so far; 'name in seen' checks all of them at once.

walk.gloss: Have we seen this name anywhere before?

fix.recommended:
dup = False
seen = set()
for name in names:
    if name in seen:
        dup = True
    seen.add(name)
print(dup)

alternatives.note: A set drops repeats, so it's shorter if there was one — the shortcut.
Your first version: correct, but checks every pair; slow on long lists.

blocks.title: A flag that stays up
blocks.teaches: Start with dup = False; the first match flips it to True, and nothing flips it back.

blocks.title: A set remembers who came by
blocks.teaches: A set keeps every name you add, once — a repeat doesn't add a second copy.
blocks.code:
seen = set()
for name in ['ana', 'ben', 'ana']:
    seen.add(name)
print(len(seen))

checkpoints.prompt: Three names went in. What gets printed?

blocks.title: One question to the set
blocks.teaches: name in seen asks the set in one step: is this name already in there?
blocks.code:
seen = {'ana', 'ben'}
print('ana' in seen, 'cy' in seen)

blocks.title: Look first, then add
blocks.teaches: Ask whether the name is in seen BEFORE you add it — otherwise every name finds itself.
blocks.code:
seen = set()
name = 'ana'
seen.add(name)
print(name in seen)

checkpoints.prompt: Only ONE ana signed in here. What gets printed?
